frontier.hypothesis: Another permuter cycle - reseeded from a STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT chassis, not from the 15-floor body - will keep moving the floor, because the preference-reachable spelling space is now proven large and only a fraction of it has been sampled.
frontier.mechanism: Preference bits (set_preference / prune_preferences, global.c:1671 / 882-931) are written off the RTL copy structure, which C-level naming and reassociation control directly; s3 confirmed the lever and s4 confirmed it is worth 15 points. The s4c basin being dry after 17k iterations is a statement about ONE starting point, not about the space.
frontier.next_probe: Rebuild from tmp/perm_23648_s4/ (validate base.o vs target.o first - it must reproduce the CURRENT sandbox residual of 15 mismatching lines at 159/159). Seed campaign A from the varK (argp, floor 17) body rather than varL, since varK is a different seat assignment at a comparable floor and its basin is completely unexplored. Seed campaign B from a hand-restructured chassis in the abs/clamp/div16 region. Use tools/permuter_annotate.py to focus randomization on the diverging region. Harvest+stop each at the no-novel-find window.

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining 15-line residual is a small, nameable set of seats that a fresh RA read can localise, exactly as s3 did for the 30-line residual - but every allocno id from s1-s3 must be re-derived first.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocates in a fixed priority order and each assignment ORs its hard reg into the conflicts of every conflicting allocno, so the whole seat map shifts when the first-allocated allocno changes; two of this session's edits sit on the region that produced ord=0.
frontier.next_probe: With the current candidate applied, run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80023648` plus BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 and BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG over the new ord list; produce a fresh 159-line aligned seat diff (the s3 scripts tmp/grind/func_80023648/s3/{allocdbg.sh,findreg.sh,diffseats.sh} still work). Then RE-STATE H9/H10 against the new ids - do NOT spend a probe on the old 129/122/86 numbering.

frontier.hypothesis: The two levers found this session generalise: variable reuse and named address intermediates are broadly effective on this function's preference structure, so a systematic sweep of BOTH over every eligible site will find further drops that random search missed.
frontier.mechanism: Both winning deltas are the same shape - give an already-computed value a second C-level identity so the RTL copy structure (and therefore set_preference's bit) changes. There are roughly a dozen more eligible sites in this body that neither the permuter's random walk nor s2/s3's enumeration has covered.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate every value in the body that is currently anonymous or single-use (the 0x1CA reads, the mult/shift chain, the sin/cos index expressions, the D8/E0 accumulates) and measure a named-intermediate and a variable-reuse spelling of each ON TOP OF the current 15-floor body, one at a time at 159/159. Measure singly first - s4 proved these levers contend rather than compose, so stacking without per-delta measurement is misleading.
